transcript.text: Good morning everyone. I've called this brief equipment-readiness check because we have one mobile bariatric lift available for immediate assignment, and both the North and South inpatient units have patients whose transfer plans are being reviewed for use of the lift. Before I finalize the assignment, hospital policy requires us to hold this check with physical therapy, facilities, nursing education, and infection prevention. I'd like to go around and hear from each of you on equipment readiness and any concerns. Who'd like to start?

transcript.text: I'd like to share my physical therapy assessment findings for both patients. The South unit patient failed the sit-to-stand assessment and requires a full-body bariatric lift for every bed-to-chair transfer. The North unit patient can currently complete a two-person stand-pivot transfer with a gait belt. Based on these clinical assessments, the South unit patient has a greater immediate need for the bariatric lift.

transcript.text: I need to share an important facilities finding. The available lift is the Titan-MB model, which has a 48-inch turning radius. This fits South room 412's 50-inch doorway, but North room 318 has a 36-inch doorway and cannot safely accommodate this lift. The charger must therefore be placed in the South 4B equipment alcove. From a facilities standpoint, this lift can only be safely assigned to the South unit.

Three South-unit nurses have completed the lift competency validation, and hospital policy requires two validated staff members for every lift transfer. Their available coverage is 07:00-19:00 daily. This means the South unit can meet the two-person competency requirement for lift transfers during those hours.
